geography: Israel (majority of affected employees; remaining locations not specified)
summary: HoneyBook is cutting around 30 to 35 employees, approximately 14% of its workforce, with most affected employees in Israel. The company explicitly linked the restructuring to aligning its structure and workflows with the AI era and integrating AI into its product and customer value proposition. This is company-stated strategic restructuring, not a claim that AI directly replaced the affected workers. The tracker uses 30, the lower end of the reported range, for aggregate totals.
evidenceQuote: HoneyBook is undergoing a reorganization process aimed at aligning our structure and workflows with the AI era, while integrating AI into our product and value proposition for customers,
notes: October 8, 2026 is the CTech/Calcalist report date. Meir Orbach reported around 30 to 35 affected employees out of a 255-person workforce and described the reduction as approximately 14%; both figures are reported approximations, not a newly calculated exact count. The numeric field records the conservative lower bound of 30, not an exact headcount. HoneyBook said the reorganization was driven by financial strength and strategic focus, with the goal of becoming faster and more agile, and explicitly connected departing employees to this process. The attribution is company-stated through a quotation in reputable reporting, not an independently obtained primary announcement. No direct AI replacement count or completed-departure date was disclosed.
